description: Structured forum + marketplace dataset of the Evolution dark web cryptomarket (carding forum + drug market, active Jan 2014-Mar 2015), plus a longitudinal weighted forum co-posting network. Boekhout, Blokland & Takes (Leiden University).
citation: Boekhout, Hanjo; Blokland, Arjan; Takes, Frank. A large-scale longitudinal structured dataset of the dark web cryptomarket Evolution (2014-2015). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10171217
license_note: Confirmed via the Zenodo API record (access_right=open, license=cc-by-4.0). Redistributable with attribution -- still kept local under external_data/ (gitignored) rather than committed, consistent with keeping third-party datasets out of git history regardless of license.

schema_notes.note: Read directly from inside data-and-readme.zip by the adapter (zipfile + csv, tab-delimited) -- not extracted to disk, to avoid doubling ~2GB of disk use for files this large (market/listings.tsv alone is 732MB uncompressed).
schema_notes.forum/forum.tsv: fid, category, title, description, topics, posts, ... -- one forum board.
schema_notes.forum/user.tsv: uid, username, reg_year/month/day, title (rank), num_posts, location -- one forum account.
schema_notes.forum/topic.tsv: fid, tid, first_uid (topic starter), title, posts, views -- one forum thread.
schema_notes.forum/post.tsv: tid, pid, uid, year/month/day/time, text (HTML), signature -- one forum post. text is real free-text content: the corpus this dataset offers for stylometry research (see Section 15 of the brief).
schema_notes.forum-market/user-matching.tsv: match_id, username, uid, vid -- Evolution's OWN linkage of one forum account (uid) to one marketplace vendor account (vid) sharing a username. This is dataset-internal ground truth about ONE PLATFORM's account linkage, not a real-world operator identity -- see safety_boundary.
schema_notes.market/vendors.tsv: vid, username, rank, sales, approval_rating, pgp_key (often a full armored PGP public key block), return_policy -- one vendor account.
schema_notes.market/listings.tsv: lid, vid, title, price, description, cid (category), ships_from/to, product_class -- one product listing.
schema_notes.market/listing-feedback.tsv: lid, username (partially redacted, e.g. 'h***k'), year/month/day, message -- one buyer feedback/review.
schema_notes.network/nodes.tsv: uid, secondary_uid, tertiary_uid, match_id, init_year/month -- forum-account identity nodes (multiple uids can be one match_id, i.e. one matched identity across account changes).
schema_notes.network/edges-2014-*.tsv, edges-2015-*.t: Source, Target, Weight, timestamp, tid -- the pre-built longitudinal weighted co-posting network: an edge between two forum users who posted in the same topic, one file per month. This is the 'communication network' the paper models -- co-posting, not a proven message exchange between the two people.

safety_boundary: user-matching.tsv links a forum uid to a market vid -- that is Evolution's own same-platform-account fact, not a CyberTrace SAME_OPERATOR claim about any investigation target. Co-posting edges model communication proximity, not verified messaging, and never imply control. See cybertrace/integrations/evolution.py docstring and tests/test_integrations.py.
